data.title: Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal dials Oil India CMD over fire at Tengakhat oil reservoirs, urges best medical treatment for injured
data.description:
Dibrugarh, Nov. 7 -- Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW) Sarbananda Sonowal spoke by telephone with the Chairman and Managing Director of Oil India Ltd. at the company's headquarters in Duliajan to take stock of the explosion and major fire at the Tengakhat oil field's ITF facility.

During the conversation, Sonowal urged the company to ensure the best medical treatment for everyone injured in the incident and to take all necessary measures without delay.

The Lok Sabha MP from Dibrugarh LSC also called for appropriate compensation for the families of those who lost their lives in the incident.

Sonowal further advocated a high-level inquiry by the concerned authorities to establish the exact cause of the fire and bring all aspects surrounding the incident to light.

Meanwhile, one worker died, and six others sustained injuries after a massive fire broke out following an explosion at the Intermediate Tank Farm (ITF) of Oil India Limited (OIL) in Tengakhat, Dibrugarh district, the company said.

This is an update to the earlier report in which five workers were reported injured, and one worker was missing following the fire and explosion at the facility on Friday morning.

The incident occurred during technical work at the facility, with preliminary reports suggesting that the explosion took place in the crude oil storage section while a valve was being operated.

Earlier, speaking to ANI, Kamal Phukan, Area Manager of Spectron Engineers Pvt Ltd, said that around five workers had sustained injuries and were shifted to Assam Medical College and Hospital (AMCH) in Dibrugarh for treatment.

"During technical work, a fire broke out and around five people were injured. They have been brought to the Assam Medical College and Hospital here. I have no information about any death," Phukan said.

In a subsequent statement, Phukan said the incident occurred during routine maintenance work on machinery that was serviced monthly or quarterly.

"There is something today that is regular, something we have to do. There was a thing called Bath Hita in Velpur. There was a machine that was serviced monthly or quarterly. There was an accident. There are 5 people in Assam Medical College, one in Oil Medical College and one whom we have not found yet. Our special team is working to find him, sir," he said.

data.title: Muyuan Foods Group, a Global Leader in Pig Farming, to Showcase Smart Pig Farming and Green Development Solutions at EuroTier 2026
data.description:
HANOVER, Germany, Nov. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- From November 10 to 13, Muyuan Foods Group (002714.SZ/02714.HK) will participate in EuroTier 2026 in Hanover, Germany. As a global leader in pig farming, Muyuan marketed 77.98 million pigs and slaughtered 28.66 million pigs in 2025. At Booth J04 in Hall 15, Muyuan will showcase integrated solutions across two key areas: Smart Pig Farming and Green Development.

Smart Pig Farming: This section will focus on pig house upgrades, biosecurity management, and intelligent equipment. Smart pig houses enable precise control of environmental parameters, while more than 30 types of intelligent equipment across five categories, including inspection robots and intelligent feeding systems, integrate key production operations into digital management systems. These solutions help improve operational efficiency, optimize costs, and drive the development of standardized and precision-driven farming practices.

Green Development: This section will feature solutions for environmental management, sterilization and deodorization, and renewable energy. Muyuan achieves 100% resource utilization of livestock manure, promoting the crop-livestock cycle and supporting a circular agricultural model. Sterilization and deodorization technologies continuously improve the farming environment, while renewable energy solutions contribute to carbon reduction and emissions mitigation. In 2025, Muyuan achieved carbon emission reductions of 6.06 million tons across its entire value chain, demonstrating its commitment to low-carbon and sustainable development.

Together, these two areas provide customers with a comprehensive, one-stop solution covering the entire pig farming process.

Throughout the exhibition, Muyuan's international business team will provide multilingual technical presentations, one-on-one business consultations, and live demonstrations of intelligent equipment. Muyuan warmly welcomes industry professionals and partners from around the world to visit Booth J04 in Hall 15. Let us work together to advance the high-quality development of the global livestock industry and explore new opportunities for cooperation!

data.title: IL JIN Electronics files draft papers for ₹2,500-crore IPO
data.description:
IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd, an arm of Amber Enterprises India Ltd, has filed preliminary papers with the market regulator SEBI to raise ₹2,500 crore through an initial public offering (IPO).

The proposed IPO is entirely a fresh issue of equity shares, with no offer for sale (OFS) component, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6.

The company plans to use the proceeds to repay or prepay certain outstanding borrowings, including accrued interest, availed by the company and its subsidiaries, Ascent Circuits and Shogini Technoarts.

The funds will also be used to purchase plant, machinery, and equipment for its manufacturing units, as well as for general corporate purposes.

IL JIN Electronics is a vertically integrated, technology-driven electronics design and manufacturing company operating across four business verticals -- electronics manufacturing services (EMS), bare printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturing, power electronics and industrial automation.

The company is a subsidiary of Amber Enterprises India Ltd, a major player in India's room air-conditioner original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and original design manufacturer (ODM) industry.

IL JIN Electronics operates 11 manufacturing facilities, including 10 in India and one in Israel. Its Indian facilities are located in Noida and Greater Noida in Uttar Pradesh, Pune in Maharashtra, Chennai and Hosur in Tamil Nadu, and Bengaluru in Karnataka.

Six additional manufacturing facilities are currently under construction and are expected to support its future capacity expansion.

On the financial front, IL JIN Electronics' revenue from operations rose to ₹3,268.47 crore in FY26 from ₹1,240.41 crore in FY24. Its EBITDA grew from ₹321.07 crore in FY26 from ₹71.42 crore in FY24.

Motilal Oswal Investment Advisors, Axis Capital and Jefferies India have been appointed as the book-running lead managers to the issue, while KFin Technologies will act as the registrar to the IPO.

data.title: Dan Ives Warns ‘No Way To Sugarcoat’ That Democrats’ Blue Wave Is Negative For AI Buildout — But Calls Tech Stocks Sell-Off ‘Irrational’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ives said investors were beginning to price in an earlier peak in capital expenditure growth, with concerns about the political environment adding to pressure on AI infrastructure companies.
  • However, he argued that the market was extrapolating the election outcome too aggressively.
  • Ives added that even if 20% of planned data centers fail to materialize, demand would still significantly outstrip supply over the next two years.

Wall Street's AI trade is facing a fresh political overhang after Democrats' sweeping midterm victories raised questions about the future of data center expansion. However, Yorkville Ives partner Dan Ives believes investors are overreacting, arguing that the AI boom remains firmly intact despite the political uncertainty.

Speaking on Bloomberg Radio and CNBC on Friday, Ives acknowledged that the Democratic victories could complicate the AI infrastructure buildout, particularly in states such as Texas. However, he pushed back against fears of a broader slowdown, calling the recent technology stock sell-off irrational and describing the pullback as a potential buying opportunity.

Blue Wave Could Slow AI Buildout, But Ives Says Investors Are Overreacting

"There was no way to sugarcoat that. The blue tidal wave. It's a negative for the AI builder," Ives told Bloomberg.

He said investors were beginning to price in an earlier peak in capital expenditure growth, with concerns about the political environment adding to pressure on AI infrastructure companies, including neocloud providers and energy players.

However, Ives argued that the market was extrapolating the election outcome too aggressively. He added that even if 20% of planned data centers fail to materialize, demand would still significantly outstrip supply over the next two years.

Ives also pushed back against concerns that semiconductor companies such as Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) would face weaker demand or have to cut their forecasts.

He estimates that 800 to 1,000 data centers would be built, adding that roughly 75% of planned projects were already permitted or under construction and therefore likely to proceed.

Ives described the AI boom as being in its early stages, comparing it to a party that is far from over despite the political disruption.

"The cops came to the party for a noise violation," Ives said, estimating that the AI party was still around 11:30 p.m. or midnight, with hours left before it ended.

Ives Calls Tech Sell-Off 'Irrational,' Sees Golden Buying Opportunity

During an interview with CNBC, Ives doubled down on his bullish outlook, arguing that investors were treating technology stocks as though the AI revolution was no longer happening.

"I think this is just irrational selling when it comes to tech," he said.

Ives pointed to semiconductor stocks, hyperscalers and software companies as examples of businesses caught up in the broader market retreat, despite the massive infrastructure spending expected to support AI adoption.

He acknowledged that capital expenditure growth could peak earlier than previously anticipated, potentially by one or two years. However, he argued that this would not invalidate the longer-term investment opportunity.

"This will be a golden buying opportunity," Ives said, particularly pointing to hyperscalers. Investors betting against the AI boom, he suggested, may be getting ahead of themselves.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 0.17%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) rose 0.21%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged up by 0.06%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

The Global X Artificial Intelligence & Technology ETF (AIQ) rose 1.32% on Friday, while the iShares U.S. Technology ETF (IYW) gained 1.31%.

data.title: Arka Fincap signs agreements with The Rise Funds for investment of an initial amount of ₹525 crore
data.description:
Arka Fincap Ltd, a Kirloskar Group-promoted non-banking financial company (NBFC), on Saturday said it has signed definitive agreements with The Rise Funds, a core pillar of TPG’s global impact investing platform, for strategic investment of an initial amount of ₹525 crore.

The definitive agreements also incorporate a potential investment for an additional ₹275 crore through a subsequent tranche, subject to the achievement of specified business milestones aligned with Arka’s growth strategy and requisite regulatory approvals, the NBFC said in a statement.

Arka, which is a diversified, secured retail lending NBFC, has assets under management (AUM) of ₹8,000 crore. It has a presence across ten states through 146 branches.

The NBFC said TPG’s investment will provide growth capital to support the evolution of business through deepening its geographical reach and accelerating investments in technology and risk management capabilities.

“With TPG’s extensive sector experience and innovative approach towards building and scaling successful financial institutions, together with Kirloskar Group’s long-term institutional commitment, deep understanding of the geography and the customer, Arka is well positioned to capitalise on the vast opportunity in India’s secured lending market,” per the statement.

Gauri Kirloskar, Vice Chairperson and Managing Director, Kirloskar Oil Engines Ltd, said: “We believe this partnership marks the beginning of a meaningful, long-term relationship that will create lasting impact for Arka, TPG and all our stakeholders, most importantly our customers across the country.”

Samrat Gupta, Managing Director, Arka Fincap Ltd, noted that Kirloskar Group’s established legacy and TPG’s global investment expertise create a trustworthy platform for Arka’s next phase of growth.

Crossing ₹1,000 crore in secured retail assets is a defining milestone in Arka’s ambition to build a formidable, future-ready financial enterprise, serving entrepreneurial aspirations of India, he added.

Simit Batra, BU Partner, TPG, observed that many of India’s MSMEs and vehicle operators remain underserved by formal financial services, and Arka has built a disciplined, secured retail lending platform to serve these customers, with the potential to reach even more customers at scale.

“We are excited to partner with the Kirloskar Group and Arka’s experienced team as the company enters its next phase of growth,” he said.

data.title: Malaysia's king warns against challenging his order allowing house arrest for ex-PM Najib
data.description:
Malaysia's king warned on Saturday that any attempt to challenge his order letting former Prime Minister Najib Razak go from jail to house arrest could amount to defying his decree, a day after authorities delayed Najib's transfer.

Najib has been in jail since 2022 after being found guilty of corruption and money laundering in a case linked to a multibillion-dollar scandal at state fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad. He has consistently denied wrongdoing.

He was due to be transferred home on Friday, after his party paid a 50-million-ringgit ($12-million) fine to fulfil a condition of a royal pardon issued by King Sultan Ibrahim in September that would allow him to serve his remaining two years at home.

The transfer, however, was suspended after the attorney-general's office said questions had arisen over the legal interpretation of the royal pardon and a court order issued on Friday allowing Najib to leave jail.

Sultan Ibrahim said on Saturday his pardon order was "clear, explicit and without any ambiguity", noting that the attorney-general and federal territories minister had attended the pardons board meeting at which the order was issued.

"There should therefore be no confusion over its interpretation, nor should there be prolonged uncertainty over the implementation of the decision that has been granted," the king said in a statement issued by the national palace.

The attorney-general's chambers did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside office hours.

The AGC responded, however, to accusations by Najib's lawyers of executive overreach, saying in a statement it was only seeking legal clarity and had "never disputed, set aside or intended to suspend the conditional pardon order granted by His Majesty."

"The AGC considers that the issue ... should be referred immediately to the court for a clear determination and directions," it said.

The king, a position held in rotation by Malaysia's nine regional sultans, plays a largely ceremonial role in Malaysia but ​has the authority to grant pardons, according to discretionary powers under the ⁠constitution.

The monarch and the country's other sultans are held in deep respect by Malaysians. Negative remarks about the royalty can be prosecuted under the colonial-era Sedition Act.

($1 = 4.0560 ringgit)

data.title: Not all fund managers follow the crowd: Here's a list of stocks that are present in only one mutual fund scheme
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Not every stock in a mutual fund portfolio is a popular pick among fund managers. While popular stocks such as HDFC Bank feature in the portfolios of over 700 mutual fund schemes, some companies find a place in just one scheme.

These relatively uncommon stock picks reflect the distinct investment strategies, market views and stock-selection approaches of individual fund managers.

According to data shared by Value Research on X, 13 stocks feature in the portfolios of just one mutual fund scheme each. These include stocks such as Simplex Infrastructures, Ambika Cotton Mills, Tourism Finance Corporation of India and Brooks Laboratories.

The data highlights how fund managers sometimes take relatively uncommon stock bets, allocating a portion of their scheme's assets to equity options that may not be widely held across the mutual fund industry.

The table lists the 13 stocks, their respective mutual fund schemes, and the percentage of each scheme's net assets allocated to the stock.

Simplex Infrastructures has the highest allocation among the listed stocks, accounting for 2.80% of Quant Infrastructure Fund's net assets. Tourism Finance Corporation of India follows with a 2.69% allocation in Union Active Momentum Fund. At the other end, Q-Line Biotech accounts for 1.08% of Abakkus Small Cap Fund's net assets.

Interestingly, Taurus Flexi Cap Fund features two stocks on the list - Ambika Cotton Mills and Regaal Resources. Taurus Ethical Fund also has two such holdings: SRIT India and Univastu India.

The stock picks are spread across different categories of mutual funds, including sectoral/ thematic funds as well as diversified equity funds such as flexi-cap and multi-cap schemes.

The list also includes one hybrid scheme, Samco Dynamic Asset Allocation Fund, which holds Steamhouse India, showing that such relatively uncommon stock picks are not limited to pure equity funds.

A stock appearing in only one mutual fund scheme reflects the fund manager's individual investment conviction and portfolio strategy. Such holdings may also offer investors exposure to stocks that are less commonly held across mutual fund portfolios, potentially reducing portfolio overlap.

However, investors should understand the fund manager's approach and assess how these stock picks fit into their overall portfolio and risk profile.

data.title: NSE to revise closing auction session, F&O trading hours from December 7
data.description:
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) has announced changes to the Closing Auction Session (CAS) in the equity cash segment and trading modalities in the equity derivatives segment, with the revised framework set to take effect from December 7.

The exchange issued two separate circulars on November 6, following the Securities and Exchange Board of India's (SEBI) October 15 review of the Closing Auction Session, market timings and settlement methodology for derivatives contracts.

The changes include shortening the closing auction session to 10 minutes, revising the methodology for determining closing prices of eligible stocks, extending derivatives trading hours to 3:45 pm and changing the calculation of expiry-day settlement prices for stock and index derivatives.

What changes in the Closing Auction Session?

Under the revised framework, the Closing Auction Session will operate from 3:30 pm to 3:40 pm on all trading days.

The session will have the following schedule:

  • 3:30 pm to 3:31 pm: Reference price calculation and transition from the Continuous Trading Session (CTS) to CAS.
  • 3:31 pm to 3:36 pm: Order entry, modification and cancellation for both market and limit orders.
  • 3:36 pm to 3:40 pm: Only limit orders can be placed, modified or cancelled. Market orders cannot be modified or cancelled. The order-entry period will close randomly during the last two minutes.
  • 3:40 pm to 3:45 pm: Order matching and trade confirmation.
  • 3:45 pm to 3:50 pm: Transition period.
  • 3:50 pm to 4 pm: Post-close session.

The CAS will continue to apply to securities for which derivative contracts are available on any stock exchange, subject to specified exceptions.

How will stock closing prices be calculated?

The reference price for securities covered under CAS will be determined using the volume-weighted average price (VWAP) of trades executed between 3:15 pm and 3:30 pm.

If no trades take place during this 15-minute period, the last traded price (LTP) of the security during the day will be considered. If there are no trades during the day, the previous trading day's closing price will be used, adjusted for corporate actions wherever applicable.

The price band during CAS will be 3% above or below the reference price.

For securities covered under CAS, the closing price will be determined through the equilibrium price discovered during the auction. If an equilibrium price is not determined, the reference price will be considered the closing price. If there is no trade in the security during the day, the latest available closing price will be considered.

Only market and limit orders will be allowed during CAS. Stop-loss and disclosed quantity orders will not be permitted. Unexecuted eligible limit orders from the continuous trading session will be carried forward to CAS, subject to the revised price band and other conditions.

What changes in equity derivatives trading hours?

The NSE has also revised trading hours for stock and index derivatives.

Under the new schedule, trading in stock derivatives will continue until 3:45 pm on all trading days, including expiry days.

For index derivatives, trading will also continue until 3:45 pm on regular trading days. However, on expiry days, trading in contracts expiring that day will stop at 3:30 pm. Other index derivatives contracts will continue to trade until 3:45 pm.

The trade modification window will remain open until 4:15 pm for both stock and index derivatives.

How will F&O price bands change?

The exchange has aligned the price bands for stock and index futures with the revised closing auction framework.

Between 3:30 pm and 3:45 pm, the price bands for stock and index futures will be set at 3% above or below their respective reference prices.

The reference price will be calculated using the VWAP of trades executed in the respective futures contracts between 3:15 pm and 3:30 pm.

If no trades take place during this period, the last traded price of the contract during the day will be considered. If there are no trades during the day, the theoretical price of the contract will be used, based on the underlying stock's cash-market price at 3:30 pm or the latest available underlying index value.

The existing methodology for options price bands and Limit Price Protection (LPP) ranges will remain unchanged throughout trading hours, including CAS.

How will expiry-day settlement prices be calculated?

The NSE has also revised the methodology for calculating final settlement prices of expiring stock and index derivatives contracts.

For expiring index derivatives, the settlement price will be based on the underlying index value calculated using the VWAP of its constituent securities during the last 30 minutes of the Continuous Trading Session in the equity cash segment, from 3 pm to 3:30 pm.

For expiring stock derivatives, the settlement price will be based on the VWAP of the underlying stock during the same 30-minute period across all stock exchanges.

The exchange has also revised the reference-price calculation and price-band framework for stock and index futures to align them with the changes in the cash segment.

The NSE said the functional changes arising from the revised framework would be available for testing during mock trading sessions. Separate circulars will be issued regarding these sessions.

data.title: Kevin O'Leary Predicts CLARITY Act Will Pass In 2027, Says Tokenization Makes Crypto Regulation An ‘Economic Necessity’
data.description:
Key points:
  • According to Kevin O'Leary, tokenization helped streamline the financial services system.
  • He explained that the money transfer system used today was as old as the 60s and needed change.
  • His prediction came as the CLARITY Act remained stalled in the Senate.

Investor Kevin O'Leary, popularly known as "Mr. Wonderful," predicted that the Digital Market Asset Clarity Act (CLARITY Act), the stalled bill that would set federal rules for U.S. crypto markets, will pass in 2027 "out of economic necessity."

O'Leary listed the passage of the CLARITY ACT among three predictions for next year. "I'm going out on a limb here," he said on Thursday. He tied his view to tokenization, saying that "Tokenization is a good idea to streamline the financial services system. It's much better than what we have now," he said.

​​https://x.com/kevinolearytv/status/2118470977956827408?s=46

O'Leary explained that much of the system for moving money was decades old. "Some of the ways we transfer money came from the 60s, and they haven't been upgraded yet," he said. "When we go to blockchain, that will solve a lot of problems."

Pressure To End Conflicts

The Clarity Act was one of three predictions O'Leary made, all built on the idea that economic pressure would force a resolution. He said the U.S. trade war with Canada would end because both economies faced a common rival. "The big adversary to the North American economy is China," he said. "So trade wars and tariffs will be gone."

He also predicted that the conflict in the Middle East would wind down, because major oil importers could not absorb prolonged high prices. "India, China, Japan, and countless other countries cannot live with oil over $100," he said, adding that he expects the Strait of Hormuz to reopen by the end of 2027.

U.S. crude traded near $91 a barrel on Friday, up 0.3% on the day. Brent stood just above $98. Crude fell nearly 12% over the week as investors weighed the risk of renewed U.S.-Iran tensions against hopes for a diplomatic deal.

Bitcoin's price was up by 0.2% during the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Bitcoin was in the 'bearish' zone, while chatter around it was at 'normal' levels over the past day.

Bill Stalled In Senate

His prediction comes as the bill's path has grown more complicated over this year. It hit a wall in the Senate in September, when a procedural vote to take it up failed 49-50, short of the 60 votes needed.

The political picture also changed this week, as Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in the midterms. That changes who will lead talks on the bill when the next Congress takes office in January.

The timing matters because each Congress lasts two years. Any bill that doesn't pass both chambers before the session ends dies and must be reintroduced. That means the Clarity Act would have to start over in the new Congress if it doesn't clear the Senate before then.

data.title: BSNL plans roaming pact with Vodafone Idea in 12-13 more telecom circles
data.description:
State-owned BSNL plans to sign an inter-circle roaming agreement with debt-ridden Vodafone Idea in 12-13 circles, a government source aware of the development said.

The pact will mutually benefit both companies by providing access to mobile signal to their respective customers where their network is weak.

"BSNL is doing ICR (inter-circle roaming) arrangements with VIL. It has already 2-3 circles and is planning to add another 12-13 circles," the source said.

While BSNL is a public sector unit, the government is the single biggest shareholder in Vodafone Idea.

The source said that BSNL is ramping up its 4G network.

"Approval has been given to BSNL to install 26,000 new 4G mobile towers," the source said.

Fresh towers are in addition to 1 lakh 4G towers already installed by BSNL.

Vi, on the other hand, is trying to raise debt to support its Rs 45,000 capital expenditure.

The company has already raised Rs 6,400 crore as the first tranche of funds, including Rs 1,183 crore from warrants and debt proceeds, through ECB and Indian private banks.

data.title: Temasek sells nearly 4% stake in CarTrade Tech for ₹470 crore
data.description:
Singapore’s state-owned investment firm Temasek on Friday divested nearly a 4 per cent stake in multi-channel auto platform CarTrade Tech for ₹470 crore through an open market transaction.

Temasek, through its affiliate MacRitchie Investments Pte Ltd, offloaded 18.20 lakh shares, representing a 3.74 per cent stake in Navi Mumbai-based CarTrade Tech, as per the bulk deal data available on the BSE.

The shares were disposed of at an average price of ₹2,583 apiece, taking the deal value to ₹470.10 crore.

Following the latest transaction, Temasek's holding through MacRitchie Investments in CarTrade has come down to 3.08 per cent from 6.82 per cent earlier.

On the buying side, US-based Capital Group through its arm SmallCap World Fund Inc and Norway's Government Pension Fund Global together bought more than 17.23 lakh shares, or 3.54 per cent, holding in CarTrade for ₹445 crore.

The shares were acquired at the same price.

Shares of CarTrade Tech rose 3.72 per cent to close at ₹2,699.30 per share on the BSE.

data.title: US stocks always rise after midterms. Is this time different?: McGeever
data.description:
By Jamie McGeever

The market meltdown following the Republicans' electoral drubbing on Tuesday could signal a rough year ahead for Wall Street. Yet history shows that US stocks typically rise in the year following midterm elections, and usually by quite a bit.

But if US President Donald Trump's second term has taught us anything, it is that many of the economic assumptions and market playbooks that shaped investor thinking for decades may no longer apply.

So as the dust settles on the landmark midterms, the question is: is this time different? Investors' immediate reaction to the Democrats' thumping victory was certainly eye-opening — Wall Street shed $3.2 trillion and US chip stocks plunged 12% in their second-biggest fall on record on Thursday — amid worries that the Democratic-controlled Congress could slow the breakneck buildout of AI data centers.

Is this nervousness a sign of things to come?

THE HISTORICAL PLAYBOOK

If history rhymes, the outlook for the year after a midterm should be positive. In the 12 months after every midterm election since 1950, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX has risen, gaining around 15% on average.

But the stock market rises over almost any 12-month period, one might argue. That's true, which makes a deeper dive into the data essential.

Since World War Two, the S&P 500 has risen in calendar years 71% of the time, posting an average gain of just over 9% and a median rise of 11.6%, according to analysts at Deutsche Bank.

So what about the 12 months after a midterm election? Between 1946 and 2022, the market was up 100% of the time after the vote, posting an average gain of 14.4% and a median return of 13.7%. That's a roughly 4- to 5-percentage-point advantage on average and around 2 points at the median.

What accounts for this? Partly, it's because of what typically happens before the midterms. The S&P 500's average rise in midterm election years since 1949 has been only 8.4%, according to Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Wealth Advisory. Uncertainty around the vote, balance-of-power shifts and policy implications builds ahead of the election and can weigh on returns.

After the vote, this uncertainty is, in theory, removed, while divided government and political gridlock reduce the likelihood of major, radical policy changes. Investors typically like that.

Lerner also notes a remarkable curiosity that helps explain the post-midterm outperformance. Since 1950, the US economy has never been in recession during the third year of a presidential term, that is, the calendar year after the midterms.

Lerner calculates that the S&P 500's average return in these years is 20.9%, significantly higher than the average in years one, two, and four across presidential cycles. While there is no single catalyst, stimulative fiscal policy enacted in the first two years often takes time to filter through, while Federal Reserve rate hikes historically just tend not to bite in that window.

CRACKS IN THE PLAYBOOK

Yet no two periods are ever the same, and there are some pretty striking differences between the current economic and market environment and those of midterms past. A few stand out.

First, the stock market has performed strongly in this midterm election year, with the S&P 500 still just 5% below its all-time high even after Thursday's selloff. That means the potential for further strong gains could be limited.

On the flip side, there is still plenty of room for more reversals. Prior to Thursday's market slump, the S&P 500's maximum drawdown this year was only 9%. That's about half the typical maximum pullback of around 18% to 19% in a midterm year, according to JPMorgan.

This is particularly important because the US stock market has never been so concentrated. Whether it's the so-called "Magnificent Seven" group of Big Tech giants, the "hyperscalers" at the heart of the AI revolution, or the dozens of "AI-adjacent" companies involved in the wider buildout, it's a fact that earnings, returns, market capitalization and investment have never revolved around so few companies.

As recent weeks have shown, even if just a handful of tech giants fail to meet the lofty expectations baked into current prices, the benchmark indices may fall sharply.

At the root of this concentration is the biggest investment boom in history. The astronomical sums being plowed into AI, expected to top $10 trillion between 2025 and 2032 by some estimates, have lifted stock prices and household wealth to record levels and, according to many observers, are inflating a huge bubble.

Parallels with the dotcom boom and bust are hard to ignore. The internet transformed the world and spawned many of today's trillion-dollar tech giants, but that journey also included overspending, hubris and "irrational exuberance" that led to the spectacular market crash a quarter of a century ago. Is the AI spending binge, and the mounting debt being raised to fund it, an even greater misallocation of capital?

Finally, there's the interest rate outlook. The Federal Reserve raised rates by a quarter of a percentage point in September, and financial markets are betting it will hike another half percentage point next year, bringing cumulative tightening to 75 basis points. Yet the average tightening cycle since 1954 has been 400 bps and lasted 23 months, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.

In other words, markets are currently positioned for the mildest tightening cycle in Fed history. That's a benign projection, especially with inflation approaching six years above target. While an AI slowdown could weigh on growth, the Fed may also find itself facing the specter of stagflation if conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine keep energy prices elevated.

Either way, Wall Street does not appear prepared for a more aggressive Fed. History offers little comfort here: post-midterm Fed policy shows no consistent playbook, with the central bank having hiked, eased or held rates steady in different cycles.

THE REVERSAL RISK

If the post-midterm pattern holds and the US avoids recession in 2027, investors could be in for a bumper year. But that's far from a certainty.

Recession isn't many people's base case for the coming year, but the turbulence rocking tech stocks right now risks triggering a deeper economic earthquake. Given how pivotal the AI investment boom is to Wall Street and the country's financial well-being, a downturn or sudden reversal could bring the "R-word" into sharp focus.

On the subject of gloomy historical footnotes, the only two exceptions to the post-midterm outperformance pattern in almost a century are 1930 and 1938. The 12 months that followed these years were marked by the Great Depression and the buildup to World War Two.

This time is different, right?

(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)

Enjoying this column? Check out Reuters Open Interest (ROI), your essential new source for global financial commentary. Follow ROI on LinkedIn, and X.

And listen to the Morning Bid daily podcast on Apple, Spotify, or the Reuters app. Subscribe to hear Reuters journalists discuss the biggest news in markets and finance seven days a week.

data.title: Environmental groups embrace AI, even as they warn of data center impacts
data.description:
Key points:
  • Environmental groups use AI to track forest fires, count wildlife
  • Many say AI's benefits currently outweigh its environmental costs
  • Some are experimenting with ways to use AI more responsibly
  • UN's COP31 climate summit to highlight tradeoffs of AI use

By Valerie Volcovici

Environmental groups worldwide are using artificial intelligence to analyze climate data, track forest fires and count endangered wildlife – embracing a technology they also warn is driving a surge in electricity demand, water use and greenhouse-gas emissions.

The contradiction is forcing these organizations to justify their AI use in carrying out missions to combat climate change or protect natural resources.

"We recognize that AI can come with environmental costs, and we need to be thoughtful about how we use it," said Ali Swanson, AI lead at the US nonprofit Conservation International. "But at a time when the climate and biodiversity crises are becoming more urgent, AI can help us move faster and make better use of the information we're collecting."

The group recently started using AI to assess hotspots detected by satellites and send real-time alerts to community forest patrols about potential wildfires in remote and environmentally sensitive parts of Cambodia.

Reuters interviewed 15 major environmental, conservation and development organizations about their AI use. All said they used the technology in some form and expressed concern about the environmental impact of the data centers powering it. The centers, filled with servers, can require vast amounts of electricity, along with water for cooling.

It's a global dilemma for individuals, governments and industries balancing AI's benefits with its enormous risks. The tradeoffs likely will grab attention at the UN's COP31 climate conference this month, when host Turkey will call on governments, businesses and other institutions to sign a pledge outlining principles to ensure AI is developed and deployed sustainably.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres wants major AI companies to publicly disclose their systems' environmental impacts.

Researchers at the United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health estimate the global data-center footprint could more than double by 2030, reaching a size about twice that of Jakarta, the Indonesian megalopolis.

The International Energy Agency, meanwhile, estimates global data centers will consume about 945 terawatt-hours of electricity annually by 2030, producing the equivalent of more than 300 million metric tons of carbon dioxide. That's double current consumption and about equal to Japan's annual electricity use.

The agency also projects that global data center water consumption will increase from about 560 billion liters (147.9 billion gallons) in 2023 to about 1.2 trillion liters (317 billion gallons) annually by 2030.

Technology giants including Microsoft , Amazon and Alphabet's Google have reported rising emissions linked in part to data center expansion, raising questions about their ability to meet their own long-term climate goals.

Amazon told Reuters its artificial-intelligence products were among the most sustainable due to the company's purchases of low-carbon energy and its efforts to use power and water efficiently.

Microsoft and Google didn't respond to requests for comment.

BREAKTHROUGHS ONCE THOUGHT IMPOSSIBLE

Many of the organizations that spoke to Reuters believe AI's benefits currently outweigh its costs because the technology is enabling work that was previously difficult, expensive or impossible.

Kenya's Save the Elephants, a partner of the Wildlife Conservation Network, said it is using machine learning to improve population surveys and study elephant communication.

Frank Pope, the group's chief executive, said an aerial survey of Kenya's largest protected area last year generated roughly 200,000 images that took nine people nine months to review manually. AI models trained on Nvidia's GeForce graphics platforms can now complete similar analyses in hours.

"The results have been eye-opening," Pope said. "We found that human surveys were missing about a third of the elephants, roughly half of zebras and giraffes, and three-quarters of oryx populations."

More accurate wildlife data can help secure financing for conservation, he said.

"Ultimately, these tools make nature measurable and therefore investable," he said. "That's a critical transformation, if we're going to conserve biodiversity at scale."

At the institute founded by the late conservation icon Jane Goodall, researchers are using AI to digitize decades of field notes about chimpanzee behavior in Tanzania's Gombe National Park.

The project was once expected to take 13-15 years because the records were written by hand using the local Kiha language and scientific shorthand.

Thanks to a tool developed with Amazon Web Services, the notes can now be scanned, translated and structured in minutes, slashing the time needed to about two years, said Lilian Pintea, the Jane Goodall Institute's vice president of conservation science.

During her lifetime, Pintea said, Goodall supported the use of AI to advance conservation science, provided people remained firmly in control of how it was used.

"AI technology should be seen as tools which are human-centered," Pintea said.

LIMITING THE ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT

Some organizations are experimenting with ways to limit the environmental impact of their AI use.

The World Resources Institute (WRI), a research group that uses AI to accelerate its climate and environmental analyses, said it limits resource-intensive applications such as generating videos and images, while caching AI query results so identical searches don't need to be reprocessed.

The US-based Nature Conservancy has adopted a similar approach. It uses AI to analyze video captured on commercial fishing vessels for information on how many fish of different species they catch. But instead of uploading huge numbers of videos to centralized data centers, it has installed AI-powered digital cameras to process information aboard the vessels, reducing energy use and data-transfer requirements, said Vienna Saccomanno, a senior scientist at the organization.

"It takes a lot of engineering to make computation on the edge possible," she said. "This was worth it to reduce both our carbon footprint and deliver these sustainability insights."

Greenpeace International said it, too, uses some AI tools, mainly because software platforms it relies upon include AI features.

It's imposing internal guidelines emphasizing transparency, human oversight and "intentional" AI use, the group said. But it would prefer to sidestep the technology due to its environmental impacts and is pushing back hard on the data center buildout.

"While other organizations are asking how to use AI responsibly, Greenpeace is asking whether it's necessary to build all these massive data centers in the first place," said Katrin Xueying Wu, a climate and energy campaigner with the organization.

Other groups now see AI as vital to effective environmental activism.

"It's our job to save the planet. If we can do that more effectively and efficiently with the limited resources we've got by using AI, then we have to seriously engage in that possibility," said Stuart Butchart, chief scientist at UK-based BirdLife International.

"If we don't do it, then we're sort of being derelict in our duty."

data.title: Cathie Wood-Led Ark Loads Up On GOOG, AMD, NVDA And Biotech Stocks — But Sells CRWV, AVGO, LLY
data.description:
Key points:
  • Alphabet featured among ARK's notable purchases, with the investment firm adding shares through its ARK Innovation and ARK Next Generation Technology ETFs.
  • ARK also continued buying into the defense and aerospace space, with shares of Kratos Defense being purchased across three ETFs.
  • Ark also added to positions in AeroVironment, Joby Aviation, Intuitive Machines and Rocket Lab.

Cathie Wood-led ARK Investment Management made fresh moves across its portfolio on Friday, adding to several high-profile technology stocks while trimming exposure to a handful of established names.

The latest round of trades touched multiple ARK ETFs, spanning artificial intelligence, semiconductors, biotechnology, defense and space-related companies. The activity also included changes to some of the firm's cryptocurrency and healthcare holdings.

ARK Loads Up On GOOG, AMD, NVDA Despite Tech Sell-Off

Alphabet Inc. (GOOG) featured among ARK's notable purchases, with the investment firm adding shares through ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) and ARK Next Generation Technology ETF (ARKW).

The buying also extended to semiconductor heavyweights Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) and Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), both of which saw additions through ARKW.

ARK also continued buying into the defense and aerospace space. Kratos Defense & Security Solutions Inc. (KTOS) was purchased across three ETFs, namely, ARKK, ARK Autonomous Technology & Robotics ETF (ARKQ) and ARK Space & Defense Innovation ETF (ARKX).

Ark added to positions in AeroVironment Inc. (AVAV), Joby Aviation Inc. (JOBY), Intuitive Machines Inc. (LUNR) and Rocket Lab Corp. (RKLB) through ARKX.

Healthcare and biotechnology names featured prominently in the buying activity as well. ARK added to Natera Inc. (NTRA) through both ARK Genomic Revolution ETF (ARKG) and ARKK, alongside purchases of Tempus AI Inc. (TEM), Twist Bioscience Corp. (TWST), 10x Genomics Inc. (TXG), Scribe Therapeutics Inc. (SCTX) and Iambic Therapeutics Inc. (IAM).

ARKW also picked up shares of Cerebras Systems Inc. (CBRS), while ARKK added to its Coinbase Global Inc. (COIN) position.

ARK's Sells

On the selling side, CoreWeave Inc. (CRWV) and Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) were among the prominent technology names trimmed through ARKK. The ETF also reduced its position in Eli Lilly & Co. (LLY), alongside sales of Teradyne Inc. (TER) and Bullish (BLSH).

Bullish was sold across three funds, namely, ARK Blockchain & Fintech Innovation ETF (ARKF), ARKK and ARKW, making it one of the more widespread reductions in Friday's trading activity.

ARK's other sales included BYD Co. Ltd. (BYDDY) through ARKQ, while ARKG reduced its holdings in CareDx Inc. (CDNA) and Personalis Inc. (PSNL). ARKX also trimmed Teradyne.

ARKK’s price rose more than 3% in Friday’s regular trading session. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around ARKK trended in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: New Zealand election voting ends, early results due shortly
data.description:
By Lucy Craymer and Alasdair Pal

Voting closed in New Zealand's general election at 7 p.m. (0600 GMT) on Saturday and early results will start to be reported shortly in a race that has remained too close to call.

Opinion polls have shown both of the two largest parties, National and Labour, have a chance of forming the next government, while they have each lost support to smaller parties that will be the key to cobbling together a coalition.

Key to the result will be whether the Opportunity Party manages to top the 5% needed to get lawmakers into Parliament, with polls indicating that if they do they will hold the balance of power.

While New Zealand’s Electoral Commission expects to report preliminary results from 50% of voting places by 10 p.m., there may be no new government until after official results are released on November 27 and coalition negotiations are concluded.

New Zealand switched to a mixed member proportional system in 1996, which means people vote for both the party and a local constituency candidate.

There are 71 constituency seats and at least 49 party seats and a party or coalition needs a majority to form a government.

Special votes, which include those from overseas voters or people outside their electorate, will not be included in the vote count until November 27. Historically, special votes have favoured the left, with parties on the right losing support following the count.

data.title: MakeMyTrip acquires majority stake in Quick Ride, enters ride-pooling business
data.description:
MakeMyTrip has acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru-based shared mobility platform Quick Ride, marking its entry into the ride-pooling segment.

The company announced the acquisition on November 6.

The Quick Ride brand and its ride-pooling business have been transferred to a newly formed entity, Co Ride Mobility Private Limited, in which MakeMyTrip has acquired a majority stake. Quick Ride's promoters will continue to lead the business.

Quick Ride connects people travelling along similar routes to facilitate shared rides, primarily for daily commutes. It operates an asset-light model and has partnerships with corporates, IT parks and business campuses.

The acquisition covers Quick Ride's brand and ride-pooling business. Its existing electric vehicle (EV) taxi business will continue to operate under the predecessor entity, iDisha Info Labs Private Limited.

MakeMyTrip said Quick Ride would be part of its ground transportation business, which also includes redBus. The company said the acquisition would expand its presence in daily urban commutes and intercity travel.

"Ride pooling gives us a presence in high-frequency daily commutes within cities, as well as intercity travel," MakeMyTrip Co-Founder and Group CEO Rajesh Magow said in a statement.

The acquisition adds to MakeMyTrip's investments and acquisitions across travel-related segments. These include Savaari in car rentals, Happay in corporate travel and expense management, and Flamingo Transworld in group holiday packages. The company has also made a minority investment in visa-processing platform Atlys.

data.title: Beyond the hectares: India’s oil palm mission must measure what it sustains
data.description:
India’s oil palm expansion is gaining momentum. According to The Hindu businessline of October 30, 2026, 55,614 hectares had been brought under the crop during the current financial year against a target of 1.19 lakh hectares—around 47 per cent. The six North-Eastern states accounted for 23,347 hectares, while nine other states contributed 32,267 hectares. The Agriculture Ministry informed Parliament in August 2026 that 2.73 lakh hectares were brought under oil palm during 2021-22 to 2025-26, against the five-year target of 6.5 lakh hectares.

The reported figures, while encouraging, also highlight an important aspect of oil palm development: should success be measured merely by hectares planted, or by hectares that survive, are maintained and eventually become productive? Area expansion is a milestone, not proof of sustainable development.

A closer look is instructive. Against a target of 36,319 hectares, the six North-Eastern states have achieved about 64 per cent. The nine states in the rest of India have covered 32,267 hectares against 82,959 hectares—about 39 per cent. Andhra Pradesh and Telangana together account for roughly 85 per cent of the area covered in these nine states. This concentration merits attention and calls for understanding why adoption is slower elsewhere.

Tamil Nadu lagging

Tamil Nadu, despite favourable conditions in several locations, has not achieved the scale or consistency of oil palm development that might have been expected. Suitability maps must be followed by assessment of farmer willingness, irrigation, land characteristics, input access, extension support and proximity to processing facilities.

Oil palm is a resilient, long-duration crop, but it is not a plant-and-forget proposition. It needs regular water, balanced nutrition, timely field operations, pest and disease management and sustained technical guidance. Water stress and inadequate maintenance can sharply depress Fresh Fruit Bunch (FFB) yields. A plantation counted at planting but subsequently neglected, abandoned or uprooted cannot be treated as a development success.

The experience of Mizoram deserves attention—not to undermine the North-East’s potential, but to learn from the past. A March 2023 review by the Mizoram Governor’s office recorded that, against approximately 26,730 hectares earlier covered under oil palm, only about 3,398 hectares were then under active cultivation. Difficult terrain, rainfed conditions, maintenance constraints and FFB evacuation challenges are among the issues. The lesson is to distinguish between area ever planted, area currently maintained, bearing area and area delivering marketable FFBs. The North-East has substantial potential, provided infrastructure and sound agronomy accompany expansion.

Clearly defined KPIs

A district or mandal target should reflect dependable irrigation, suitable land, farmer readiness, quality planting material, extension manpower, access to credit and viable FFB evacuation and processing arrangements. Where these conditions are not yet in place, the answer may be phased development—not merely a higher planting target.

The businessline report also notes that fund utilisation under the scheme was below 40 per cent of the amount released at the time of reporting. Were plantations maintained? Was irrigation installed and functional? Were extension visits, survival assessments and FFB collection arrangements in place? Financial and physical progress must translate into measurable benefits in farmers’ fields.

The National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm recognises the need for support towards maintenance, drip irrigation, quality planting material, nurseries, replanting and processing infrastructure. However, monitoring must go beyond reporting area expansion and track, state-wise and age-wise, plantation survival, irrigation coverage, adherence to recommended agronomic practices, progression into bearing and FFB productivity, alongside farmer returns and effective procurement and processing. Clearly defined Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), supported by systematic field-level checklists, should assess not merely what has been planted, but how effectively plantations are being nurtured towards sustainable productivity.

Making progress visible

Above all, farmer confidence will determine the durability of this mission. Oil palm involves a long-term commitment and investment: regular FFB production generally begins only after three to four years, making maintenance during the non-bearing period critical. Uncertainty about water, inputs, technical support, procurement, prices and eventual returns can weaken a farmer’s willingness to invest and maintain the crop. Such uncertainty cannot be removed through assurances or targets alone. It must be addressed through functioning model plots, credible demonstrations, regular field visits, transparent procurement and pricing arrangements, and prompt corrective action.

A plantation-wise checklist, coupled with age-wise KPIs on survival, irrigation, maintenance and FFB yield, can make progress visible to farmers and implementing agencies. This is how knowledge becomes confidence, confidence encourages adoption, and adoption leads to transformation. Organisations should communicate a realistic time horizon and a credible value proposition: what support farmers can expect, when plantations are likely to become productive, and what commercial arrangements will sustain them. Expectations must be realistic and backed by delivery. The same discipline is needed in established as well as emerging oil palm regions.

India has a compelling reason to develop domestic oil palm production and reduce dependence on imported edible oils. The opportunity is real, including in the North-East and other growing states. But the measure of achievement must evolve. Let us count not only hectares planted, but hectares that survive, hectares that bear, tonnes of FFB produced and income sustained for farmers.

The real success of the mission will not be determined by how quickly we expand oil palm’s footprint only, but by how well we nurture it into productive, remunerative and enduring plantations.

The author is former CEO- Oil Plam Plantation, Godrej Agrovet Ltd. and Consultant-Palm Oil Production & Plantation Development, Kolkata, West Bengal.

data.title: Markets Espresso: Yeh public hai...sab jaanti hai
data.description:
Hello Espresso Lovers! Before we begin, wishing you all a very, very Happy Diwali, a prosperous New Year, and may Samvat 2083 bring everything that the year gone by could not - gains in the portfolio, less volatility, more peace, and happiness, food and laughter everywhere!

The lyricists of the generation gone by were visionaries PRO MAX. The lines they wrote, the songs they created, hold truth and relevance even in today's context. One of the most prolific of them all, was Anand Bakshi. One of the most popular songs he wrote is the theme of today's episode - Yeh Jo Public Hai Yeh Sab Jaanti Hai from Manmohan Desai's Roti (1974). The lines from that song came true not in India, but in the proverbial Saat Samandar Paar in the US, based on the turn of events over the last week!

Which were those lines?

Heere Moti tumne chupaaye, kuch hum log na bole

Par Aata, Chawal bhi chupa, to bhooko ne muh khole!

For a better part of the first two years of Donald Trump's presidency, there were plenty of reports of conflicts of interest, his sons' business interests, his own crypto dealings, the construction of the White House ballroom, and many other such things that don't really impact the life of a common American. The markets were doing well (he loves to brag about it), and the economy continued to grow on a stable footing.

Then came the Iran war.

Oil prices soared, gasoline costs were at a record high, inflation started to surge, the Fed began to hike interest rates, and the people's pockets started to get pinched. Add to that was the blinding expansion spree of data centres and the citizens losing power and getting inflated bills. Of course, there were protests and so on, but that made no difference to the lives of either billionaires or the administration. What could have been a better way to answer?

The ballot box. Team Trump was handed a resounding defeat in the midterm polls, and the Democrats not only grabbed a majority in the Senate, but also in the House of Representatives. Suddenly, all of those words that Donald Trump thought were a hoax - Climate Change, Ozone, Rising Temperatures- sprung back to life. The Nasdaq saw its biggest single-day value erosion on record, and the chances of the AI bubble coming apart are now more than ever!

Another line from the same song summed up the state of affairs.

Kya Neta, Kya Abhineta, De Janta Ko jo Dhoka

Pal Me Shohrat Ud jaaye, Jyon Ek Pawan Ka Jhonka

It cannot be more ironic that these lines not only fit Donald Trump and his current situation, but also were relevant to the hero on whom the song was filmed: Rajesh Khanna!

Samvat 2082 feels like one of two parts. 358 days of Part 1 and the final seven days of Part 2. The dead and dormant Indian market, particularly the largecaps, have come alive and how as Diwali festivities drew closer. The FIIs, the proverbial wedding uncles who are always upset over something or the other, have some newfound love for the country and our markets. After selling, selling and then some more, they have poured in nearly ₹50,000 crore over the last six sessions. You can almost hear them sing - Aaj Phir Tumpe Pyaar Aaya Hai, Behad Aur Beshumaar Aaya Hai from Dayavaan (1988)!

What has been the result of this Behad and Beshumaar Pyaar? A 22,500 Nifty just towards the end of October is now above 25,000 in just seven days! And when the largecaps ran, it was a proper team effort. Reliance Industries on Monday, Banks on Tuesday and Friday, NBFCs and Financials on Wednesday, and of course, the falling oil prices through the week, contributed to the bullish sentiment. Not to forget, most of the corporate results have been better-than-expected this time around, and no better way to get a market to run than earnings!

The Nifty jumped 7.5% in the week gone by. The last time it did so? February 2021. Yup, it's been a while. Another Nifty 50 constituent saw a week similar to the Nifty, and in fact, was a leading contributor to the index recovery too! HDFC Bank. 14% gains in the last week. The last time it did so? February 2021. If the Nifty had to run, it needed both Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma to deliver. They did, and how! If HDFC Bank was Rohit Sharma, Reliance Industries was Virat Kohli. 13% higher in the week gone by, the biggest single-day gain on Monday in six years, the highest market cap addition on record, many more records were broken on the day Reliance surged 12% after its results. If both of them continue to have such century-like weeks, who knows- maybe, just maybe, a record high on the Nifty before the year ends? For all those saying Aapke Muh Me Ghee Shakkar, I prefer Biryani!

Yes, yes, I know it's the festive time, so I would not take much longer either. But cannot close this episode out without tipping our hats to India's retail population. Their faith, their conviction, that the market will eventually wake up from its slumber. Of course, we are still far from being out of the woods, but these last seven days have ensured that the hope continues to flicker, and if things quieten down in West Asia, oil prices fall, the AI trade continues to unwind, there could well be more firecrackers in store for Samvat 2083! And as the great Javed Akhtar wrote for possibly one of the greatest films of all time - Lagaan (2001) - Sach Aur Saahas hai, jiske mann me, Ant me Jeet usi ki hogi!

Once again, from all of us at CNBC-TV18, wishing you all a very, very happy Diwali and a Wonderful, joyous, peaceful and multibagger Samvat 2083. Do like, share, subscribe and follow us on our social media handles. We'll be back next Saturday, which happens to be Children's Day! Until then, do take good care of yourselves! Ciao!

data.title: "When will action be taken?": Rahul Gandhi targets Centre over E20 petrol row
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 7 -- Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Saturday questioned the Centre over alleged excess ethanol content in petrol sold across Karnataka, asking when action would be taken against oil companies supplying fuel beyond the prescribed 20 per cent limit.

In a post on X, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi alleged that laboratory tests of petrol samples collected by the Karnataka government from seven districts showed ethanol content exceeding the prescribed limit in several samples.

"E20 turns into '420' (a scam) - Petrol theft from the public's vehicles! The Modi government claims that petrol contains 20% ethanol. The Karnataka government collected petrol samples from 7 districts and had them tested at an accredited laboratory," he said.

Referring to the test findings, Rahul Gandhi said 11 out of 14 samples contained more than 20 per cent ethanol, with IOCL samples recording 31.2 per cent and HPCL samples recording 30.5 per cent.

He further alleged that the ethanol content exceeded the prescribed limit in samples from both public and private oil companies, including Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), Nayara and Shell.

"Furthermore, the companies' own internal labs did not even report the ethanol content," he wrote.

Raising concerns over the impact on consumers, the Congress leader alleged that higher ethanol content could lead to reduced mileage and increased vehicle maintenance costs.

"In short: you are paying for expensive petrol, but your tank is being filled with ethanol. Who suffers the loss? You do...Your vehicle is not designed to handle such high levels of ethanol-this leads to reduced mileage and frequent trips to the mechanic. Your prized vehicle is being ruined," he said.

He also questioned the absence of information at fuel stations regarding the actual ethanol content in petrol, alleging that consumers were not being given a choice.

"Moreover, there is no mention at the fuel pumps regarding what is actually being put into your tank-you have no choice in the matter," he said.

Questioning Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the issue, Rahul Gandhi sought clarification on the actual ethanol content in petrol supplied across the country and demanded action against companies allegedly exceeding the prescribed limit.

"Modi ji, tell us-what exactly is being poured into the nation's fuel tanks? How much ethanol is truly in the petrol? When will action be taken against the companies that are adulterating fuel beyond the 20% limit?" he said.

He also reiterated his challenge for a debate with the Prime Minister, saying the issue should be included among the subjects for discussion. "And the challenge for a debate still stands. Let's add this issue to the list: who is actually benefiting from your policies?" Rahul Gandhi added.

His remarks come after Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL), the three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs), on Friday said they had taken note of a press release issued by the Department of Food, Civil Supplies, Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology, Government of Karnataka.

The Karnataka department had claimed that petrol sold at certain retail outlets in the state contained between 26 per cent and 31 per cent ethanol.

However, the three OMCs rejected the reported findings, stating that the claims were not supported by testing conducted in accordance with the prescribed statutory and technical procedures.

"E20 petrol supplied by the three OMCs across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline," the companies said in an official statement.

The OMCs also raised concerns regarding the sampling procedure and methodology adopted for the October 2026 exercise.

Citing the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, read with the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024, the companies said the regulations prescribe a defined procedure for sampling, retention, testing and communication of results.

According to the prescribed procedure, six one-litre samples are required to be drawn. Two samples must be handed over to the dealer against acknowledgement, two retained by the oil company or the department concerned, and the remaining two sent to a laboratory specified under Schedule III of the Control Order or notified in the Official Gazette.

The companies further stated that sample labels are required to be jointly signed and test results communicated to the dealer and the oil company within the prescribed timeframe.

The three OMCs have requested the Karnataka government to share the complete sampling documentation, outlet-wise laboratory reports and details of the testing methodology adopted for the reported findings.

They have also sought access to the counterpart samples for independent testing at an authorised laboratory using the prescribed referee method, in the presence of representatives of the State Government and the OMCs. The companies maintained that E20 petrol supplied by them conforms to the applicable BIS specifications and sought independent testing to address the concerns raised over the reported ethanol levels.

Launching a sharp attack on the Central government over fuel quality standards, Karnataka Minister G Parameshwara questioned "who is protecting consumers" after independent tests in the state allegedly revealed ethanol content in petrol reaching levels as high as 31.2 per cent-significantly higher than the mandated E20 blend.

In a post on X, the Karnataka minister raised serious concerns over vehicle safety, fuel efficiency, and consumer rights, demanding an immediate probe into the matter. He also sought an explanation from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari.

data.title: Saudi coalition intercepts Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh
data.description:
The Saudi-led coalition reported the interception and destruction of a Houthi-launched cruise missile aimed at Riyadh. This incident marks another episode in the ongoing conflict between the Saudi coalition and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi movement. The missile was reportedly neutralized before reaching its target, amid rising tensions and an increase in hostilities following the breakdown of an informal ceasefire. The coalition's actions suggest a heightened focus on air defense in response to the renewed Houthi attacks.

  • The interception of the missile appears consistent with increased military tensions between Saudi Arabia and the Houthi movement.
  • Activity indicates that this event may increase the perceived likelihood of Saudi authorities considering an airspace closure for security reasons.
  • Recent developments are consistent with scenarios where continued military escalations could impact regional stability and air travel.

Observers will be closely watching for any announcements from the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) or Saudi Air Navigation Services (SANS) regarding potential airspace closures. Statements or actions by key actors such as Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman Al Saud and Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree could further influence perceptions. The situation remains fluid, and any additional missile threats or interceptions may reinforce the current trajectory toward heightened defensive measures in Saudi Arabia.

data.title: BlackRock ETF clients sell $403M worth of Bitcoin
data.description:
Investors in BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) pulled roughly $403 million worth of Bitcoin out of the fund in a single day.

Fund flow data for November 2, 2026 put IBIT's net outflow at $405.3 million. That was the largest one-day redemption for the fund since June 26 of this year.

Estimates of the client-driven selling land between $403 million and $405 million. The precise figure depends on whose tally you use.

The mechanics matter here. BlackRock did not decide to dump Bitcoin. Its clients redeemed their ETF shares, and the fund had to release the matching amount of Bitcoin to settle those positions.

Those released coins mostly went to Coinbase Prime, the institutional brokerage arm of Coinbase, where they were sold. So the Bitcoin did end up hitting the market. It just got there because of investor decisions, not a call from BlackRock's trading desk.

Across the full lineup of US spot Bitcoin ETFs, net outflows came to about $398.6 million that day. One fund bucked the trend. Fidelity's Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) recorded a modest inflow of $6.7 million.

IBIT's $405.3 million in outflows, offset by FBTC's $6.7 million in inflows, lands almost exactly on the sector-wide total. BlackRock's fund accounted for essentially all of the day's net selling pressure among US spot Bitcoin ETFs.

This was not an isolated bad afternoon. The November 2 redemption extended a five-session outflow streak for IBIT, with cumulative withdrawals over that stretch exceeding $1 billion.

The streak ran into early November alongside a selloff in tech stocks led by the Nasdaq.

Bitcoin itself has been stuck in a fairly tight band, trading between $76,000 and $80,000.

For all the red ink, IBIT remains the largest US spot Bitcoin ETF. It leads the category both by assets under management and by total historical net inflows.

The most direct effect is on supply. Every redemption that ends with coins being sold through Coinbase Prime adds Bitcoin to the market. With cumulative IBIT redemptions topping $1 billion in just five sessions, that extra supply could weigh on prices if demand from other buyers does not keep pace.

The selling clustered heavily in one fund while Fidelity's FBTC managed a small inflow. That may point to investors reshuffling which products they hold, or to a particular set of IBIT holders deciding to step back, rather than a uniform exit from the asset class.

The comparison point to keep in mind is June 26, the last time IBIT saw a single-day redemption this large.

data.title: Mike McGlone Doubles Down On $10K Bitcoin Doom Call: 'Stock Bear Market Has Started'
data.description:
Key points:
  • McGlone first predicted the decline in Q1 2025, when Bitcoin traded above $100,000, and said a 20% S&P 500 correction could start it.
  • The index is currently about 6% below its 52-week high.
  • Scott Melker said that the stock sell-off had not hit Bitcoin as hard as bears had expected. 

Mike McGlone, Senior Commodity Strategist at Bloomberg Intelligence, doubled down on his call for Bitcoin (BTC) to fall to $10,000, saying that he believes the next stock bear market has already started.

McGlone said he had first made the call in the first quarter of 2025, when Bitcoin traded above $100,000, and said that the outlook had remained unchanged.

"The call from 1Q25 with Bitcoin above $100,000 was for it to lose a zero, on the back of a 20% drawdown in the S&P 500 (SPX) that stays down awhile, remains my base case," he wrote on X on Friday.

A Bitcoin price that "loses a zero" would fall about 90%, to roughly $10,000. McGlone said that level carried the weight for the asset, noting that "10,000 Bitcoin is a key pivot."

He also drew a link between crypto and stocks, saying that Bitcoin peaked on October 6 last year, while the Nasdaq peaked exactly a year later, on October 6, 2026.

“May the market gods be with us all when we have the next stock bear market. I think it has started," he said.

Bitcoin's price was trading at $75,830, up 0.2% during the past 24 hours, while the S&P 500 closed at 7,376 points on Friday, about 6% below its 52-week high of 7,844. That was well short of the 20% drop McGlone said would push Bitcoin toward $10,000.

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Bitcoin was in the 'bearish' zone, while chatter around it was at 'normal' levels over the past day.

Melker Questions The Thesis

McGlone's post came in response to crypto trader and well-known investor Scott Melker, famously known as the "Wolf of All Streets." He said that the stock sell-off had not hit Bitcoin as hard as bears had expected. "Nasdaq entered correction territory today, more than 10% below its recent high," Melker said on X.

Melker said the market had already covered half the drop that was meant to drag Bitcoin down. "The Nasdaq is down 10%, and we're still 17 or $18,000 above Bitcoin's low," he said.

"The case that the Nasdaq or the market dropping 20% would send Bitcoin to $10,000, to me, or something way lower right now does not make any sense because we're halfway there."

data.title: Edelweiss urges India to scrap foreign capital gains tax to revive markets
data.description:
India should consider removing the capital gains tax imposed on foreigners to help revive the country’s stock market, Edelweiss Financial Services Ltd. Chairman and Managing Director Rashesh Shah said, adding to a growing clamor for the exemption to boost inflows and support the local currency.

“We need to showcase to the foreigners we want them,” Shah said in an interview with Bloomberg Television’s Menaka Doshi and Haslinda Amin in Mumbai on Friday. “If India wants foreign investors to come back, we want India to be a good permanent allocation for foreigners, we should do something and removing capital gains tax for foreigners might be an easier answer.”

Shah joins dozens who are pushing the government to exempt foreign portfolio investors from paying long-term capital gains tax on listed equities. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said earlier this week that she will consider tax changes on stocks, but stopped short of confirming whether the government was looking at revisions to capital gains or transaction taxes.

Long-term gains on listed equities held for more than a year are taxed at 12.5 per cent, while short-term gains are levied 20 per cent.

Foreign investors have been relentless sellers of Indian stocks, with net outflows exceeding $28 billion so far this year, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. But a sharp selloff in global artificial-intelligence stocks and a decline in oil prices have prompted some overseas funds to return to the market. Foreign investors have poured in more than $5 billion into Indian equities over the past three weeks, helping drive a nearly 10 per cent rebound in the domestic market, data show.

Oil prices and any global risk-off plays are the biggest risks for Indian stocks, Shah said, but added that strong domestic inflows provide support during such times.

Shah estimates that Indian mutual funds could channel about $40 billion to $50 billion annually into equities, while insurance companies and pension funds could contribute another $20 billion to $25 billion. That would translate into new annual domestic equity inflows of roughly $60 billion to $80 billion, he said. A steady supply of domestic capital has created an opportunity for companies to raise more money through initial public offerings, according to Shah.

The Edelweiss group is planning an IPO for its asset management business in the next 18 to 24 months, Shah said. Group firm Edelweiss Mutual Fund, which manages assets worth 1.8 trillion rupees ($19 billion), counts US private equity firm WestBridge Capital as a key investor. Group firm EAAA India Alternatives began trading this week following an IPO that raised 12 billion rupees.

“We want all our underlying businesses, insurance companies, asset management to eventually IPO and get listed in the market,” he said.
